🎙
Remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at the plenary session of the 23rd annual meeting of the Valdai Discussion Club
(Moscow, October 1, 2026)
This year’s theme is
“Responsibility for the Future: Limits of the Possible, or Limitless Possibilities?”
Key
talking points:
•
Responsibility for our shared future is far more than just an abstract sloga
n. It entails a set of practical measures aimed at preventing humanity from being pushed to the brink of survival and averting irreparable consequences.
• Humanity has not yet fully comprehended the true magnitude of the challenge it faces.
We are entering a completely new and unprecedented reality
. Threats and dangers are inextricably intertwined with opportunities and prospects; they cannot be separated from one another. Our entire way of living is changing.
• Whatever scenario unfolds in the world in the years ahead, the
international conflicts, unfortunately, are likely to continue
. This is due in part to the fact that the profound shifts now under way, and the opportunities they create, fuel and encourage ambitions and a willingness to take risks for what may appear to be a major payoff.
• In the long term, as the
world moves away from Western hegemony
, the international situation will gradually improve leading to a more stable, democratic, and free multipolar international order. It is equally clear, however, that on the path towards such a world order, states, communities and every individual will face various risks.
• The UN, even if it is the most representative international organisation, falls short of the collective and democratic principles in the way it is being managed compared to its original design. A n
arrow grouping of Western countries
wields an unproportionally large influence. It constitutes a global minority by all accounts while seeking to appropriate administrative functions.
• The principle of
"might makes right"
sometimes seems to guide certain international players who are convinced of their own military-political, economic, and, as they believe, moral
exceptionalism
. We know well from history that this never leads to anything good.
• The truth is that it was not we who wanted or started the war —
it was started against us
. There was no need to encourage aggressive nationalism and Russophobia in Ukraine for years in order to turn it into a tool for fighting Russia.
• Russia was deliberately placed in a situation where it was
simply forced
— in response to this obvious aggression —
to defend itself with arms in hand
. We were deliberately brought to this line. And in general, there is no need to turn Russophobia, the oppression and killing of Russian people, and the destruction of Russia into a state ideology and to set the goal of Russia's strategic defeat.
• If we want to live — everyone wants to live — then, as I once said in a public speech,
let us live in friendship and together seek ways to make that happen
.

#NoStatuteOfLimitations
On October 1, 1946 —
8️⃣
0️⃣
years ago — the International Military Tribunal (IMT) in
#Nuremberg
concluded its proceedings
against the senior officials of the Third Reich responsible for unleashing the bloodiest and most horrific conflict in human history, committing genocide and murdering millions of innocent people.
❗️
#NurembergTrials
were an unprecedented international tribunal in history, which truly became a
"Trial of Nations" against absolute evil
— Hitler's Nazism.
The IMT's verdict in Nuremberg made a crucial contribution to the legal consolidation of the outcome of
#WW2
and declared the
Nazi misanthropic ideology,
principal organisational structures and practices of Nazism
as a whole to be entirely
criminal.
The
high-ranking leaders of Hitler's regime,
including Göring, Hess, Ribbentrop, Kaltenbrunner, Rosenberg, Keitel, Neurath, Jodl, Dönitz and other senior officials of the Third Reich —
were placed on dock.
Bormann, who had evaded prosecution, was tried in absentia.
💬
Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov
, in an
interview
for the documentary '
Nuremberg
'
(Moscow, 16 November 2025):
The question of ensuring that Nazi criminals would inevitably be brought to justice was first officially raised in a Soviet diplomatic note in November 1941.
The Soviet Union <...> was the principal initiator and driving force behind the establishment of the Nuremberg Tribunal.
Our proposals were heard and accepted.
Our country's key role
in arranging the Nuremberg proceedings is absolutely indisputable.
The Nuremberg Trials involved an enormous amount of paper work. A total of 403 public hearings were held. 116 witnesses were examined, and more than 300'000 testimonies were considered. Approximately 3,000 documents were examined.
❗️
The Trials' proceedings
elucidated
, for the first time, the
unprecedented scale of Nazi Germany's war crimes
, including the brutal treatment of POWs and the deliberate destruction of entire cities, villages and their inhabitants.
💬
Russian MFA Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova:
Although the
term 'genocide'
does not appear in the text of the Nuremberg Tribunal's Charter or verdict (it became established in international legal practice at a later date), the trial records unequivocally point to numerous acts aimed at the deliberate extermination of the Soviet people, including the years-long
siege of Leningrad.
<...>
Unfortunately, we are compelled to acknowledge that, 80 years on,
many have forgotten the lessons of the 'Trials of Nations'
. This applies not only to the Kiev regime's leadership, which, since 2014, has outlawed and sought to eradicate everything Russian in Russia's historical territories,
rehabilitating
,
glorifying
and drawing inspiration from the example of
Hitler's
collaborators
.
The same applies to those who justify, shield and support the terrorist actions of the current neo-fascist regime in Ukraine.
(From the briefing by Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, 1 October 2026)
⚖️
On 1 October 1946, a historic verdict was delivered — 19 defendants were found guilty.
Göring, Ribbentrop, Keitel, Kaltenbrunner, Rosenberg, Jodl, Bormann (in absentia) and other representatives of the Nazi leadership were sentenced to death by hanging. A number of institutions of Hitler's Germany, including the
SS,
SD
,
Gestapo
and the
Nazi
Party
leadership corps, were declared
criminal organisations.
✍️
From article by Valery Zorkin, Chairman of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation,
"The Sacred Beacon of Nuremberg and the Shadow of The Hague"
(October 1, 2026):
Nuremberg was an act of retribution against Evil and a defining moment in establishing the legal foundations of the post-war world.
The Tribunal became a hammer brought down upon a criminal state and its legal order.
#Nuremberg80

item.title: ❌ London continues its pointless sanctions policy against our country. This time, illegal restrictions have been imposed on commercial vessels, as well as on Russian nationals and
item.description: ❌ London continues its pointless sanctions policy against our country. This time, illegal restrictions have been imposed on commercial vessels, as well as on Russian nationals and organisations whom the British authorities baselessly accuse of violating the rights of Ukrainians and of “militarising” children. The “children’s issue” is being exploited with particular cynicism – now under the pretext that Russia is allegedly indoctrinating “millions of minors” in the new regions and stripping them of their identity. These claims do not stand up to scrutiny. One need only look at Ukraine itself, where the Russian language, spoken by millions of people, is banned, the canonical Orthodox Church is persecuted, monuments are destroyed and streets are renamed. What is this if not an attempt by Kiev to erase historical and cultural identity? The UK government’s reliance on pressure and escalation instead of dialogue merely demonstrates its lack of interest in a political and diplomatic settlement of the Ukraine conflict. It is naive to believe that yet another tightening of sanctions will change anything: Russia is calmly adapting to the restrictions and will continue to pursue the goals of the special military operation. Meanwhile, London’s anti-Russian course and its support for the Kiev regime have tangible consequences for ordinary Britons. Record diesel prices in the UK are clear evidence of this.

📆
On October 1, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov
held separate bilateral meetings and a trilateral meeting
with Foreign Minister of the Republic of Abkhazia Oleg Bartsits and Acting Foreign Minister of the Republic of South Ossetia Akhsar Dzhioev in Moscow.
Sergey Lavrov expressed appreciation for
the assistance provided by the Abkhazian and South Ossetian authorities in organising voting for Russian citizens
residing in the two republics in
the elections to the 9th convocation of the State Duma of the Russian Federation
.
The Ministers reaffirmed the three countries’ commitment to deepening their allied relations
. Particular attention was paid to implementing the directives issued by the Presidents of Russia and Abkhazia, and Russia and South Ossetia, following
their meetings
, including the bilateral talks held in Moscow on May 9.
The separate ministerial consultations focused on
implementing joint projects across various areas
, expanding the legal framework for bilateral relations and coordinating foreign policy efforts, with an emphasis on strengthening the republics’ standing on the world stage.
During the trilateral meeting, the Ministers
discussed global and regional issues of mutual interest
. They expressed support for maintaining regular direct dialogue between Abkhazia and South Ossetia and Georgia within
the International Discussions on Security and Stability in the South Caucasus
.
The Ministers discussed ways to advance shared priorities within
this negotiating mechanism
, including reaching an agreement on guarantees of the non-use of force between Georgia, Abkhazia and South Ossetia, as well as on launching the process of formalising the borders between Georgia and its neighbours under international law.
🤝
The ministerial talks reaffirmed the high level of mutual understanding and trust between Moscow, Sukhum and Tskhinval and contributed to further expanding cooperation.
#RussiaAbkhazia
#RussiaSouthOssetia

item.content:encoded:

🎙
Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s
opening remarks
during talks with Acting Foreign Minister of the Republic of South Ossetia Akhsar Dzhioev
(Moscow, October 1, 2026)
💬
It has become a good tradition for us to meet shortly after
the commemorative dates
celebrated by our South Ossetian allies, including
the anniversary of Russia’s recognition of the Republic of South Ossetia’s independence
on August 26, the anniversary of
the establishment of diplomatic relations
on September 9 and, of course,
South Ossetia’s national holiday – Republic Day on September 20
. Congratulations on all these occasions.
Today, we have a good opportunity to discuss
the current state and prospects of our bilateral relations
following another event that also took place in September. On September 18, your country held
an early presidential election
, won by Acting Head of State and Prime Minister
Marat Kambolov
, who took office on September 30.
A few days before his inauguration, on September 19, President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
spoke with him over the telephone
. We share the assessment of the many international observers that
the election was legitimate and free of any violations
.
We will continue working closely with President
Marat Kambolov’s
Government to deepen our allied relations.
📈
Our relations are developing positively. Bilateral trade grew by almost 15% in 2025
.
South Ossetia’s State Programme for Socioeconomic Development
is being implemented with support from the Moscow Government. New agreements have been reached on cooperation in modernising transport infrastructure, including the Nizhny Zaramag checkpoint on the Russia-South Ossetia border, and on healthcare, education and cultural projects.
All of this helps strengthen humanitarian ties
, which the peoples of Russia and South Ossetia are keen to develop.
We welcome your country’s openness to cooperation with
all international partners willing to engage constructively
. Representatives of Belarus, Nicaragua, Venezuela, Mexico, Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, South Africa, Türkiye and Germany took part in observing South Ossetia’s presidential election.
My prepared remarks say
“even Germany”
, but the explanation is clear:
in all these countries
, as in others,
there are public figures and non-governmental organisations that have no interest in bringing ideology into international relations
. They want to develop good-neighbourly ties – and broader ties beyond their immediate neighbours – with countries that share this interest.
We understand and welcome this.
Of course, the participation of representatives from so many countries shows that
the Republic of South Ossetia is known internationally
. We will continue to provide
diplomatic support
to help your country translate this recognition and visibility into concrete economic and humanitarian projects involving a wider range of foreign partners.
🤝
Today, following
the telephone conversation between our Presidents
,
we will review our bilateral relations
. We will also take stock of developments on the external front, which I have already touched upon. Then, together with
Abkhazia’s Foreign Minister Oleg Bartsits
, we will discuss matters related to
the International Discussions on Security and Stability in the South Caucasus
, which concern the interests of all three of our countries.
#RussiaSouthOssetia

item.title: 🎙 Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s opening remarks during talks with Foreign Minister of the Republic of Abkhazia Oleg Bartsits
item.description: 🎙 Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s opening remarks during talks with Foreign Minister of the Republic of Abkhazia Oleg Bartsits (Moscow, October 1, 2026) 💬 First of all, we would like to congratulate you on Abkhazia's Victory and Independence Day , which you celebrated yesterday. President of Russia Vladimir Putin sent his congratulations on this occasion. We cherish this chapter of our modern history. Turning to our bilateral relations, they are developing dynamically . A key event in 2026 was the meeting between Presidents Vladimir Putin and Badra Gunba in Moscow on May 9. They agreed to expand our bilateral cooperation and identified specific socioeconomic and humanitarian projects. This sets a practical agenda for all of us , with our Ministries playing a coordinating role, as stipulated in our Presidents’ decrees. Today, we will discuss in detail the progress of our joint work on the international stage . We note that major initiatives are being implemented, including the reconstruction of embankment in Sukhum, hot meals in schools and a new hub for the We Are Together NGO . These projects truly reflect the realities of our relations today, the affinity between our peoples and the friendship that binds them. 📈 We see considerable potential for investment cooperation , as demonstrated by the First Abkhazian International Economic Forum . We will continue to develop this area. It is encouraging that bilateral trade grew by 16% in 2025 . This is a very good result.

💬
First of all, we would like to congratulate you on
Abkhazia's
Victory and Independence Day
, which you celebrated yesterday. President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
sent his congratulations
on this occasion. We cherish this chapter of our modern history.
Turning to our bilateral relations, they are developing dynamically
. A key event in 2026 was
the meeting
between Presidents
Vladimir Putin
and
Badra Gunba
in Moscow on May 9. They agreed to expand our bilateral cooperation and identified specific socioeconomic and humanitarian projects.
This sets a practical agenda for all of us
, with our Ministries playing a coordinating role, as stipulated in our Presidents’ decrees.
Today, we will discuss in detail the progress of our joint work on the international stage
. We note that major initiatives are being implemented, including the reconstruction of embankment in Sukhum, hot meals in schools and a new hub for
the We Are Together NGO
. These projects truly reflect the realities of our relations today, the affinity between our peoples and the friendship that binds them.
📈
We see considerable potential for investment cooperation
, as demonstrated by
the First Abkhazian International Economic Forum
. We will continue to develop this area. It is encouraging that
bilateral trade grew by 16% in 2025
. This is a very good result.
Abkhazia is a popular destination for Russian tourists
. The number of excursions to your country
has already increased by more than 40% in 2026
. President of Abkhazia
Badra Gunba
has said that he aims to ensure that
the Republic welcomes five million visitors annually by 2030
. We will certainly do everything we can to help achieve this target. Naturally, this will require investment in infrastructure and measures to ensure safety and security.
We will support independent Abkhazia’s development in every area without exception
, including domestic development, external relations and coordination on the international stage.
Speaking of international affairs, I know that you recently visited
the Syrian Arab Republic
. I would be grateful to hear your impressions and plans.
🤝
We will review all the issues on our agenda and later with our colleague from South Ossetia
Akhsar Dzhioev
discuss
current international issues and regional security
, including
the International Discussions on Security and Stability in the South Caucasus
. This format requires our constant attention. I therefore believe that our meeting today is very timely.
